local.h: Court tosses lobstermen's suit against aquarium
local.b: A federal appeals court sided with the Monterey Bay Aquarium in a defamation suit by Maine lobstermen over its Seafood Watch advice not to buy lobster.
local.title: Appeals court dismisses Maine lobstermen defamation case against California aquarium

local.h: Brigham nurses postpone strike to vote on offer
local.b: Brigham and Women's Hospital nurses postponed a strike planned for Wednesday after a 13-hour bargaining session. Negotiators will bring the hospital's latest offer to all 4,000 union members.

local.h: Birds of prey adapt to Chicago's poles and towers
local.b: Raptors are using street lights, electric poles and cell towers to survive and in some cases thrive in the Chicago region, a sign some are back from the brink.
local.title: Many birds of prey are finding utility in lamp posts, electric poles and cell towers in Chicago region

local.h: Serbian Orthodox church heads toward landmark status
local.b: St. Simeon Mirotočivi Serbian Orthodox Church at 3737 E. 114th St., built in 1969 as a faithful interpretation of an ancient Serbian church, is heading toward city landmark status.
local.title: Orthodox church modeled after 15th century monastery heads toward landmark status

local.h: Youth conference honors Rev. Jesse Jackson
local.b: Omega Psi Phi's 10th District hosted a youth leadership and STEM event at Rainbow PUSH Coalition on Jackson's birthday weekend, honoring the late civil rights leader.
local.title: Omega Psi Phi Fraternity, Rainbow PUSH celebrate Rev. Jesse Jackson’s birthday with youth conference

local.h: LA plans Olympics watch parties
local.b: Building on its free World Cup watch parties, Los Angeles will host watch parties for the 2028 Olympic Games.
local.title: LA will host Olympics watch parties. Here’s where they might be

local.h: Long Beach residents fight high surf to save homes
local.b: Waves fueled by Tropical Storm Rachel are slamming the Peninsula's bulkhead in Long Beach, where crews and residents have reinforced defenses with boards and braces.
local.title: Long Beach Peninsula residents join scramble to save homes from high surf

local.h: Hochul declares measles 'disaster' emergency
local.b: Gov. Kathy Hochul declared a disaster emergency over the spread of measles in New York.
local.title: NY measles spread prompts 'disaster' emergency. It didn't have to be this way, health commissioner says.

local.h: Man shot by ICE still has bullet in neck
local.b: The man shot by ICE agents in New York City last week remained in solitary confinement at a Brooklyn federal lockup with a bullet lodged in his neck, his attorneys said.
local.title: Man shot by ICE in NYC still has bullet lodged in neck, attorneys say

local.h: Mamdani orders review of NYPD force policies
local.b: Facing criticism from the left over his approach to policing, Mayor Mamdani announced a comprehensive review of the NYPD's use of force policies.
local.title: Mayor Mamdani orders review of NYPD use of force policies

local.h: NYPD Bomb Squad contractor faced LI scrutiny
local.b: A company that won a $23 million contract to build an NYPD Bomb Squad building in the Bronx was flagged in a 2020 Nassau County inspector general report for not disclosing who ran the business.
local.title: Company that won $23M NYPD building contract was investigated by LI watchdog

local.h: Mamdani: ICE agent looked like a mass shooter
local.b: Mayor Zohran Mamdani said the plainclothes ICE agent with a long gun who shot a Dominican immigrant in the Bronx could easily have been mistaken for a mass shooter.
local.title: Plainclothes ICE agent with long gun looked like mass shooter, Mayor Mamdani says

local.h: NJ Transit faces 5 weeks of disruptions
local.b: Starting Sunday, NJ Transit rail lines will see cancellations, new departure times and stopping changes as crews move the final track to the new $2.3 billion Portal North Bridge.
local.title: NJ Transit riders face 5 weeks of schedule disruptions starting Sunday

local.h: Cyberattack forces supermarket fridge shutdowns
local.b: E. Leclerc, Intermarché and Coopérative U said a cyberattack caused refrigerators to defrost in hundreds of stores, forcing spoiled food to be thrown away.
local.title: French supermarkets suffer refrigerator shutdown after 'unprecedented' cyberattack

local.h: Headmaster, teacher shot at school near Marseille
local.b: A 14-year-old was arrested after a headmaster and teacher were shot with a hunting rifle at a middle school in Aubagne. Police said their lives were not in danger.
local.title: Headmaster and teacher shot inside French secondary school

local.h: Fire destroys Paris's oldest covered market
local.b: An overnight fire destroyed the Marché Couvert des Enfants Rouges in the Marais, a street food venue that has stood in the same space since 1615, authorities said.

local.h: Glucksmann wins centre-left presidential primary
local.b: Euro MP Raphaël Glucksmann won 66 percent of the 120,787 votes in the centre-left primary, becoming its candidate for next year's French presidential election. Socialist leader Olivier Faure was second with 14 percent.

local.h: Macron's popularity hits record low
local.b: Just 15 percent of respondents held a favourable view of President Macron in an Ipsos BVA-Cesi poll, the lowest score of his presidency.

local.h: Ireland proposes €140bn cut to EU budget
local.b: Ireland, holding the EU presidency, suggested cutting the bloc's next proposed budget by 140 billion euros to bridge divisions and reach a deal by year's end.

local.h: Scammers used AI to impersonate KUOW reporter
local.b: KUOW's Katie Campbell describes scam emails sent in her name and how to avoid AI impersonation traps.
local.title: Scammers used AI to impersonate me, a KUOW reporter. Here’s how to avoid such traps
